# ADR-0003: Model skill identity as name, id, and plugin name

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Bifrost gateways identify skills by a **raw repository name** (for example `git-release`),
which is used in HTTP routes such as `/api/skills/serve/{skill}/download.zip`.
Claude Code marketplaces prefix plugin names with `bifrost-` (for example
`bifrost-git-release`). OpenCode identifies and loads a skill by its **installed directory
name**, which is kebab-case.

Users may refer to the same skill using any of these forms, and catalog sources expose
different fields. The domain model must keep the concepts distinct while accepting all forms.

## Decision

- Maintain three identity fields in the domain model:
  - `name`: raw Bifrost skill name, used for HTTP routes and persisted in markers.
  - `id`: kebab-case OpenCode skill id, used as the installed directory name and for
    `@skill-id` references.
  - `plugin`: optional Claude Code marketplace plugin name (`bifrost-<name>`), present when
    the catalog came from a marketplace manifest.
- Derive/sanitize ids with `skillId()`: NFKD-normalize, strip diacritics, lowercase, keep
  `[a-z0-9._-]`, collapse multiple dashes, trim leading/trailing dashes or dots, and fall back
  to `bifrost-skill` when the result is empty.
- Resolve user input by matching `name`, `id`, or `plugin` against the catalog when available.
- When downloading, try a list of candidate names (original, stripped of `bifrost-`, plugin
  name) and continue on HTTP 404; other errors abort.
- Persist both `name` and `id` in `.bifrost-skill.json` so updates and removals can match
  records reliably.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Flexible user input: raw name, `bifrost-*` name, or installed id all work.
  - Stable on-disk identity for OpenCode discovery and `@skill-id` usage.
  - Resilience to naming differences across catalog sources and gateway configurations.
- **Negative**
  - Ambiguity must be handled carefully; multi-skill archives are matched by catalog entry and
    fail as corrupt when a package cannot be determined.
  - Normalization is lossy by design, so distinct raw names could theoretically collide to the
    same id.
- **Notes**
  - The fallback id `bifrost-skill` exists only to avoid invalid empty names; such skills are
    unlikely in practice.

# ADR-0012: Use only public skill routes; no management credentials

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

The Bifrost gateway exposes two credential planes:

- **Inference** (`/v1/*`, `/openai/*`, `/anthropic/*`, …) — uses virtual keys (`sk-bf-…`) or
  provider keys. This is what users typically have in their `BIFROST_API_KEY` environment
  variable.
- **Management** (`/api/*`) — the dashboard/control plane: config, providers, virtual keys,
  teams/budgets, MCP servers, plugins, logs, governance, and the Skills Repository CRUD. Per
  Bifrost's docs it accepts a **management API key**, a **dashboard session token**, or
  **admin Basic auth** — and explicitly **not** virtual keys or `x-api-key`.

The plugin previously used the management API (`GET /api/skills`) as a catalog source to
obtain names, descriptions, versions and pagination. This required users to provide a
management key, which they would not do for a CLI feature that should work without dashboard
access.

## Decision

- **Remove all management API integration.** Only the public routes are used:
  - `GET /api/skills/serve/claude-code/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (optional, per-skill
    metadata with versions)
  - `GET /api/skills/serve/all/download.zip` (public, names and versions from `SKILL.md`)
  - `GET /api/skills/serve/{skill}/download.zip` (public, per-skill install)
- **Remove credentials handling entirely.** No `apiKey`, no `BIFROST_API_KEY`, no secret
  storage, no masking, no auth headers.
- **Legacy key scrub.** When reading plugin storage, any `apiKey` property is silently
  removed to avoid accumulation.
- **Tombstone for old commands.** `/bifrost-config` still parses `apiKey`, `--api-key`,
  `clearApiKey`, etc. as options, but fails with a clear message if any is present.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - No dashboard credentials required for any operation.
  - No credentials in plugin storage, environment variables, config files or logs.
  - Aligns with Bifrost's design: the public download routes exist so CLI agents can fetch
    skills without carrying dashboard credentials.
  - Eliminates the confusing 401/403 errors users encountered when their virtual key was
    rejected on management endpoints.
- **Negative**
  - Loss of server-side pagination (handled adequately client-side for normal sizes).
  - Loss of visibility into skills that exist in the repository but aren't served (which
    users generally can't install anyway).
- **Migration**
  - Users with `BIFROST_API_KEY` set can leave it; it simply becomes unused.
  - Plugin options that contain `apiKey` can be removed.
  - Legacy keys in plugin storage are automatically scrubbed on first read.

## Notes

- The plugin continues to provide the full feature set: catalog browsing, install,
  install-all, list, update, remove and config. The only difference is that no management
  credential is needed or accepted.
- This is a breaking change for any users who relied on the management API for catalog
  enrichment, but those cases are rare (the public bundle already provides names and
  descriptions).

# opencode-bifrost-skills

[![Build Status](https://github.com/bitExpert/opencode-bifrost-skills/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/bitExpert/opencode-bifrost-skills/actions)
[![Mastodon Follow](https://img.shields.io/mastodon/follow/109408681246972700?domain=https://rheinneckar.social)](https://rheinneckar.social/@bitexpert)

Discover and install [Agent Skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/) from a
[Bifrost](https://docs.getbifrost.ai/features/skills-repository) gateway's Skills
Repository into OpenCode 2 — globally or per project.

The plugin adds a `/bifrost-*` command family and an interactive skills
browser. It writes skills into the directories OpenCode already scans, so an
installed skill is immediately available through the `skill` tool and
`@skill-id` mentions. The commands themselves do not ask the model to do
anything; they perform the install and post the result into the session.

## Features

- Interactive catalog browser (`/bifrost-skills`) with search and
  global/project scope picker.
- Non-interactive install, install-all, list, update, remove and config
  commands.
- Global scope (`<config dir>/skills`) and project scope
  (`<project>/.opencode/skills`).
- Catalog fallbacks that keep working when the gateway's marketplace manifest
  is unavailable.
- Refuses to overwrite by default; updates compare versions and content hashes.
- Validates every archive (path traversal, entry count, per-file and total
  size) and installs through an atomic staging directory.
- No build step: the package exports TypeScript sources that OpenCode's Bun
  runtime loads directly.

## Requirements

- OpenCode 2.x (verified against 2.2.5).
- A Bifrost gateway that serves the public skill download routes under
  `/api/skills/serve/…`.
- Bun for development and tests (OpenCode already bundles its own runtime).

## Install the plugin

Add the package to the `plugins` array in your OpenCode config
(`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` by default, or the project's
`opencode.json`):

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills"]
}
```

A single entry loads all parts of the package: the server plugin, the TUI
plugin (`/bifrost-skills`) and the typed RPC contract. A published package
name works the same way.

To pass options, use the object form:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills",
      "options": {
        "baseUrl": "https://bifrost.example.com",
        "timeoutMs": 20000
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Supported options: `baseUrl`, `timeoutMs`.

Restart OpenCode (or reload plugins) after changing the config. The commands
then appear in slash completion under `/bifrost-…`.

## Quick start

```text
/bifrost-config baseUrl=https://bifrost.example.com
/bifrost-skills
```

Install a single skill:

```text
/bifrost-install git-release --project
```

Or install all skills:

```text
/bifrost-install
# or explicitly:
/bifrost-install all
/bifrost-install *
```

After an install, use the skill with `@git-release` or let the `skill` tool load
it when the task matches its description.

## Commands

| Command                           | Arguments and flags                   | Description                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/bifrost-skills`                 | —                                     | Browse the catalog, pick a scope, install. Asks before replacing an existing skill and offers to install another. |
| `/bifrost-install [<skill>\|all]` | `--global` \| `--project`, `--force`  | Install one skill (by name) or all skills from the all-skills bundle. Defaults to `all` if no selector given.     |
| `/bifrost-list`                   | —                                     | List installed Bifrost skills in both global and project scope.                                                   |
| `/bifrost-update [<skill>\|all]`  | `--global` \| `--project`             | Update installed skills. Defaults to `all` and checks the global and session project scopes.                      |
| `/bifrost-remove <skill>`         | `--global` \| `--project`             | Remove an installed skill. Scope is required when the skill exists in both.                                       |
| `/bifrost-config`                 | `baseUrl=…`, `timeoutMs=…`, `--reset` | Show or change gateway settings.                                                                                  |

### Flag notes

- `--project` writes into the session's project; `--global` writes into the
  OpenCode config directory. Install commands default to `--global`.
- `--force` replaces an existing skill without refusing. Without it, install
  reports that the skill is already installed.
- `/bifrost-list` and `/bifrost-update` inspect the global scope and the
  session's project scope. Scope flags narrow update and remove, not list.
- Skill names may be given as the raw Bifrost name (`git-release`), the
  marketplace plugin name (`bifrost-git-release`) or the installed skill id.
- For batch installs, use no argument, `all`, or `*` as the selector.
- Option spellings are flexible: `baseUrl=…` / `--base-url …` /
  `--url …`, `timeoutMs=…` / `--timeout-ms …`.

## Where skills are installed

| Scope   | Directory                                                                           |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Global  | `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/skills`, else `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/opencode/skills` |
| Project | `<session directory>/.opencode/skills`                                              |

The project directory is resolved on the server from the session that ran the
command (`session.location.directory`), not from the TUI process's working
directory. A project install therefore follows the session even when the
OpenCode UI was started elsewhere.

Each skill directory contains the downloaded files plus a
`.bifrost-skill.json` marker with its id, source, scope, version, content hash
and timestamps. The marker is how the plugin recognises its own installations.
The commands only populate these directories — loading is OpenCode's job.

## How the catalog is discovered

The client tries two sources in order and uses the first non-empty result:

1. **Marketplace manifest** —
   `GET /api/skills/serve/claude-code/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
   Provides names, descriptions and versions. The gateway only serves it when
   `client.skills_external_client_url` is configured and `git` is available.
2. **All-skills bundle** — `GET /api/skills/serve/all/download.zip`, public.
   Names, descriptions and versions are read from each `SKILL.md` frontmatter.

Installs do not depend on the catalog: they always use
`GET /api/skills/serve/{skill}/download.zip`, with the all-skills bundle for
batch installs (no selector, `all`, or `*`). Installing by name keeps working when every catalog
source is unavailable.

If the catalog cannot be read at all, the command still supports
`/bifrost-install <name>`; the download route decides whether the name exists.

## Install and update behaviour

**Install** downloads the archive, validates it, writes every file into a
hidden staging directory next to the target, writes the marker, then renames
the staging directory into place. Replacing an existing skill keeps a backup
until the new directory is in place, so a failed install does not leave a
half-written skill behind.

- An existing directory is only replaced with `--force` (or after confirming
  in the marketplace dialog).
- A directory without a Bifrost marker is treated as foreign and is refused
  without `--force`.
- After a successful install the plugin asks OpenCode to reload its skill
  registry.

**Update** (`/bifrost-update`, default `all`):

- Reads the installed markers from both scopes.
- Compares the gateway version with the installed version. If the installed
  copy is newer, it is left alone.
- Downloads the current archive and compares a SHA-256 content hash over file
  names and contents. Identical content is reported as unchanged even when
  versions differ.
- Newer or different content is installed through the same staging path and
  the marker keeps its original `installedAt` while gaining `updatedAt`.

Updates replace the whole skill directory. Local edits inside an installed
skill are not merged and are lost when that skill is updated or replaced.

**Remove** deletes only directories that contain a valid Bifrost marker and
live directly inside a known skills root. If the same skill exists globally
and in the project, `--global` or `--project` is required.

## Configuration

Settings are resolved with this precedence (highest first):

1. **Command override** — passed by the TUI/RPC for a single call.
2. **Plugin storage** — written by `/bifrost-config`.
3. **Plugin options** — the `options` object in the OpenCode config.
4. **Environment** — `BIFROST_URL`, `BIFROST_TIMEOUT_MS`.
5. **Default** — `http://localhost:8080`, 20 000 ms.

`/bifrost-config` shows the effective values and where each one came from.

```text
/bifrost-config
/bifrost-config baseUrl=https://bifrost.example.com timeoutMs=15000
/bifrost-config --reset
```

The gateway URL is normalized: a missing scheme becomes `http://`, trailing
slashes are removed, a trailing `/api` is stripped, and URLs containing
credentials are rejected (use `baseUrl` instead).

## Security

- Archive entries with absolute paths, `..` segments, backslashes or paths that
  resolve outside the skill directory are rejected.
- Limits: 64 MiB archive, 2 000 entries, 8 MiB per file, 64 MiB uncompressed
  total. Empty or corrupt archives fail with a clear message. The response body
  is streamed under the request timeout with a running byte cap, so a stalled
  or oversized download can neither hang the command nor exhaust memory.
- Files are written inside a staging directory under the skills root; nothing
  is written outside it. Files starting with a shebang keep the executable bit
  (`0755`); everything else is written `0644`.
- Remove refuses unmarked directories and paths that are not direct children of
  a skills root.
- Installed skills are data, not trusted code: they can contain instructions
  and helper scripts. Review a skill before installing it from an untrusted
  gateway, and remember that the agent may follow its instructions.

## Development

```bash
bun install
bun test            # 82 tests, Bun's built-in runner
npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
npm run check       # both
```

### Package layout

| Path                | Purpose                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/index.ts`      | Server plugin: RPC handlers, `/bifrost-*` command registration, notices.                      |
| `src/tui.tsx`       | TUI plugin: interactive `/bifrost-skills` dialog and toasts.                                  |
| `src/rpc.ts`        | Typed RPC contract and JSON schemas shared by both parts.                                     |
| `src/bifrost.ts`    | HTTP client, catalog fallbacks, error types, URL normalisation.                               |
| `src/operations.ts` | Install/install-all/update/remove/list, staging, markers, hashing.                            |
| `src/settings.ts`   | Settings precedence, skills directories, config summary.                                      |
| `src/zip.ts`        | Zip decoding, path/size validation, package grouping, hashing.                                |
| `src/args.ts`       | Parser for slash-command arguments and option aliases.                                        |
| `src/format.ts`     | Markdown rendering of command results.                                                        |
| `src/types.ts`      | Shared record and result types.                                                               |
| `test/`             | Bun tests with in-memory storage and a mock gateway (one test uses a real local HTTP server). |

### Package exports

```jsonc
{
  "exports": {
    ".": "./src/index.ts", // server plugin
    "./tui": "./src/tui.tsx", // TUI plugin
    "./rpc": "./src/rpc.ts" // typed RPC contract
  }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                    | What to check                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Browser shows “Could not reach …”          | Run `/bifrost-config`, confirm the gateway URL and that it is reachable from the OpenCode host.                                                                   |
| Catalog is empty but install by name works | The gateway may not serve a marketplace manifest; `/bifrost-install <name>` still uses the public download route.                                                 |
| “already installed … use --force”          | Use `--force`, `/bifrost-update <skill>`, or remove it first.                                                                                                     |
| `/bifrost-list` is empty                   | Confirm the skill directory contains `.bifrost-skill.json` and that you are in the project that owns a project-scope install.                                     |
| A skill does not appear in `@` completion  | Wait for the reload after install, then check the directory name equals the skill id. Global and project directories are scanned by OpenCode, not by this plugin. |
| Commands are missing from slash completion | The plugin entry/path is wrong, or OpenCode was not restarted after the config change.                                                                            |

# Architecture Decision Records

This directory contains Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for `opencode-bifrost-skills`.

## Purpose

ADRs document important design decisions, the context in which they were made, the chosen
alternatives, and the consequences of the choice. They are intended to make the project's
rationale easier to discover and discuss.

## Conventions

- Each ADR is a single Markdown file named `NNNN-short-title.md`, where `NNNN` is a
  zero-padded sequence number.
- ADRs use a lightweight MADR-inspired structure: **Status**, **Context**, **Decision**, and
  **Consequences**.
- New decisions should get the next available number; existing ADRs are not renumbered.
- When a decision is superseded, mark the old ADR **Superseded** and link to the replacement.

## Current ADRs

| ADR  | Title                                                                                       | Status     |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| 0001 | [Distribute as a no-build TypeScript OpenCode plugin package](0001-no-build-plugin.md)      | Proposed   |
| 0002 | [Split server plugin, TUI plugin, and shared RPC contract](0002-plugin-split.md)            | Proposed   |
| 0003 | [Model skill identity as name, id, and plugin name](0003-skill-identity.md)                 | Proposed   |
| 0004 | [Support global and project install scopes](0004-install-scopes.md)                         | Proposed   |
| 0005 | [Use multi-source catalog fallback with catalog-independent installs](0005-catalog.md)      | Superseded |
| 0006 | [Validate archives and enforce bounded downloads](0006-archive-validation.md)               | Proposed   |
| 0007 | [Install atomically with staging, markers, and content hashes](0007-atomic-install.md)      | Proposed   |
| 0008 | [Use conservative update and removal semantics](0008-update-removal.md)                     | Proposed   |
| 0009 | [Resolve configuration with precedence, normalization, and secret handling](0009-config.md) | Superseded |
| 0010 | [Provide forgiving slash commands with non-model transcript reporting](0010-commands.md)    | Superseded |
| 0011 | [Use minimal runtime dependencies and Bun-native tooling](0011-dependencies.md)             | Proposed   |
| 0012 | [Use only public skill routes; no management credentials](0012-public-skill-routes.md)      | Proposed   |
| 0013 | [Unified install slash command](0013-unified-install-command.md)                            | Proposed   |

## Notes

- The ADRs in this repository describe decisions already implemented in the codebase, so
  their status is **Proposed** until formally reviewed and accepted.
- Where an ADR mentions package metadata inconsistencies (for example repository vs. homepage
  URLs), those are documentation/hygiene items and may be addressed without creating a new ADR.
- ADRs 0010, 0012 supersede earlier management API usage. ADR 0013 unifies install commands.

# ADR-0001: Distribute as a no-build TypeScript OpenCode plugin package

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

OpenCode 2 plugins run on OpenCode's Bun-based runtime and can load TypeScript/TSX sources
directly. The project provides three public surfaces (server plugin, TUI plugin, RPC contract)
and needs to be easy to develop, test, and consume.

A full transpile/build step would add tooling, create separate `dist/` artifacts, and introduce
the risk of published code diverging from the source tested in CI.

## Decision

- Publish the npm package with **source-level exports**, not built artifacts:
  - `.` → `./src/index.ts` (server plugin)
  - `./tui` → `./src/tui.tsx` (TUI plugin)
  - `./rpc` → `./src/rpc.ts` (typed RPC contract)
- Keep `files` limited to `src`, `README.md`, and `LICENSE`.
- Require Bun for development and tests (`engines.bun >= 1.2`), while relying on OpenCode's
  bundled runtime to execute the plugin in production.
- Use strict TypeScript (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride`,
  `isolatedModules`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`) with `noEmit`.
- Use Biome for linting and a single `npm run check` command (`lint`, `typecheck`, `test`) for
  CI and local validation.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Single source of truth: the code shipped, tested, and reviewed is identical.
  - Simple packaging and release flow (no build artifacts to publish).
  - Fast local workflow: `bun test` and `tsc --noEmit` run directly against sources.
- **Negative**
  - Consumers must run a runtime that can load TS/TSX (true for OpenCode).
  - The package is not usable as an ordinary Node library without transpilation.
- **Notes**
  - `package.json` currently mixes GitHub and GitLab URLs (repository/CI vs. homepage/issues).
    Aligning those is a separate metadata/hygiene decision, not a change to this ADR.

# ADR-0002: Split server plugin, TUI plugin, and shared RPC contract

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Installing skills from a Bifrost gateway involves privileged and potentially long-running
operations: HTTP requests, settings persistence, filesystem writes, and reloading OpenCode's
skill registry. The same plugin also needs an interactive catalog browser with dialogs,
toasts, and search.

OpenCode separates server-side plugin capabilities from TUI interactions. Placing all logic
in one component would make it hard to reason about trust boundaries, reuse operations, and
avoid slash-command naming collisions.

## Decision

- **Server part** (`src/index.ts`, backed by `Operations`):
  - Owns the Bifrost HTTP client, settings resolution/storage, archive validation,
    filesystem writes, and registry reloads.
  - Registers all non-interactive `/bifrost-*` slash commands.
  - Executes commands directly and reports results by emitting a `notice` event and appending
    a synthetic session message to the transcript without waking the model.
- **TUI part** (`src/tui.tsx`):
  - Owns the interactive `/bifrost-skills` command (catalog browser with search, scope
    selection, overwrite confirmation, and "install another" loop).
  - Consumes server functionality through the typed RPC contract and reacts to `notice` events
    with toasts.
- **Shared RPC contract** (`src/rpc.ts`, `BifrostRpc`):
  - Defines typed methods for `catalog`, `install`, `installAll`, `list`, `update`, `remove`,
    and `config`, plus a `notice` event schema.
  - Uses explicit object schemas (close to JSON Schema) to keep TUI and server in sync.
- **Operations** (`src/operations.ts`) are a framework-agnostic domain service used by both the
  server commands and RPC handlers, making behavior testable with mocked gateways/storage.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Clear trust/ownership boundary: network and filesystem mutations live in one place.
  - Reusable operations for slash commands and UI flows.
  - Avoids command-name collisions and keeps interactive UI in the TUI where dialogs/toasts
    are available.
- **Negative**
  - More moving parts: the RPC schemas and domain types must be kept aligned.
  - The TUI relies on specific OpenCode context APIs and data shapes
    (`session`, `location`, `ui.dialog`, `ui.toast`, `data.location.skill.invalidate`);
    plugin API changes may require coordinated updates.
- **Notes**
  - The server's synthetic message approach ensures command outcomes appear in chat history
    without triggering model inference.

# ADR-0004: Support global and project install scopes

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Users need skills either available in every project or only in a specific workspace.
OpenCode scans fixed skill locations, and the TUI process's current working directory may
differ from the active session's project directory. Project-scoped operations must therefore
target the correct workspace reliably.

## Decision

- Support two scopes:
  - `global`: install under the OpenCode config directory:
    - `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/skills` when set.
    - `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/opencode/skills` otherwise.
  - `project`: install under the session/project directory at
    `<directory>/.opencode/skills`.
- For slash commands, resolve the project directory **on the server** from the invoking
  session (`ctx.session.get(sessionID).location.directory`), not from the process working
  directory. The TUI resolves the directory from its current route/session/location data.
- Default install commands to `global`; `project` requires an available directory and errors
  with guidance when it cannot be resolved.
- List and update inspect both global and project scopes (when a project directory is known),
  while remove requires an explicit scope when the same skill exists in both to avoid
  accidental cross-scope deletion.
- Only directories recognized by a valid Bifrost marker are considered plugin-managed (see
  ADR-0007).

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Predictable alignment with OpenCode's skill discovery.
  - Global skills are reusable across projects; project skills stay with a workspace.
  - Resolving project scope from session state keeps installs correct even when OpenCode's
    UI was started elsewhere.
- **Negative**
  - Project operations depend on session/location data being available and up to date.
  - Dual-scope listing makes commands aware of more state, which must be explained in output.
- **Tradeoff**
  - Mutation commands favor explicit scoping (`--global`/`--project`) while read/update
    commands inspect both scopes for convenience.

# ADR-0005: Use multi-source catalog fallback with catalog-independent installs

- **Status:** Superseded by ADR-0012
- **Amended:** 2026-11-16
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Bifrost gateways vary in capabilities:

- The marketplace manifest may only be served when an external client URL is configured and
  `git` is available.
- Public per-skill and all-skills zip routes are commonly available and sufficient for
  installing a known skill.

Catalog metadata (descriptions, versions) is useful for browsing but is not strictly required
to install. Partial failures (404/503, parsing issues, empty responses) should not
block core functionality.

## Decision

- Build the catalog by trying sources in order and returning the **first non-empty** result:
  1. **Marketplace manifest**
     `GET /api/skills/serve/claude-code/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`
  2. **All-skills bundle**
     `GET /api/skills/serve/all/download.zip` (metadata read from `SKILL.md` frontmatter)
- Collect non-fatal issues in `Catalog.warnings`; each source produces a warning when it
  fails.
- Deduplicate and sort catalog entries by name.
- **Installs are catalog-independent:**
  - A named install always uses the public per-skill route
    `GET /api/skills/serve/{skill}/download.zip`.
  - `/bifrost-install-all` prefers the all-skills bundle and falls back to the catalog plus
    per-skill downloads when the bundle is empty or unusable.
- If no catalog source is available, commands still allow `/bifrost-install <name>`; the
  download endpoint is authoritative.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Works across heterogeneous gateway configurations and degraded states.
  - Users receive warnings instead of hard failures when richer catalog metadata is
    unavailable.
  - Core install capability remains available even when catalog endpoints are down.
  - No management API credentials required.
- **Negative**
  - Metadata richness varies by source (versions and descriptions may be missing).
  - Probing multiple endpoints increases request volume and code complexity.
- **Notes**
  - The catalog `source` field (`marketplace`, `zip`) is surfaced in TUI titles and
    formatters so users can see which fallback was used.

# ADR-0006: Validate archives and enforce bounded downloads

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Skill archives are untrusted network input and are unpacked to disk. The main risks are
path traversal (zip-slip), resource exhaustion (large or numerous entries), stalled
downloads, and corrupt or malformed archives.

The plugin must therefore validate archives and downloads before and during processing, and
must fail with clear, typed errors.

## Decision

- Decode ZIP archives using `fflate` and enforce hard limits:
  - **64 MiB** maximum archive/download body size.
  - **2,000** maximum entries.
  - **8 MiB** maximum size per file.
  - **64 MiB** maximum total uncompressed size.
- Validate entry names with `normalizeEntryName()`:
  - Reject NUL bytes.
  - Reject absolute paths and drive-letter prefixes.
  - Reject `..` traversal segments.
  - Normalize backslashes to forward slashes and strip empty segments.
  - Ignore directory entries.
- Download response bodies with streaming:
  - Apply the request timeout to both header retrieval and body reading.
  - Keep a running byte total and abort when it exceeds the 64 MiB cap.
  - Honor caller-provided `AbortSignal`s for cancellation.
- Require a `SKILL.md` file in a package; fail as `corrupt` when it is missing.
- Parse `SKILL.md` frontmatter leniently: invalid YAML is treated as no frontmatter, and the
  file still installs.
- Use typed errors with stable codes (`BifrostError` and `ZipError`) such as `network`,
  `timeout`, `cancelled`, `unauthorized`, `not-found`, `unavailable`, `http`, `corrupt`,
  `unsafe-path`, `too-large`, `too-many-files`, so UI and formatters can report consistent
  messages.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Strong defense-in-depth against common zip-slip and DoS vectors.
  - Predictable failure modes with user-friendly error messages.
  - Stalled or oversized downloads cannot hang the command or exhaust memory before the caps
    apply.
- **Negative**
  - Legitimately large or unusually structured skills are rejected.
  - Some ZIP metadata (for example Unix permission bits) is not trusted or exposed; executable
    bits are derived from content (see ADR-0007).
- **Tradeoff**
  - Lenient frontmatter parsing favors availability over strict metadata correctness.

# ADR-0007: Install atomically with staging, markers, and content hashes

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

OpenCode loads skills directly from directories. Partial writes or interrupted installs can
leave a half-written skill directory, which would be loaded as broken content. The plugin must
also distinguish its own managed installs from foreign/manual content and detect "unchanged"
updates reliably.

Archives from the network do not provide trustworthy executable-bit metadata, so the plugin
must choose file modes deterministically.

## Decision

- Install flow:
  1. Create a hidden **staging directory** under the skills root, named
     `.bifrost-staging-<id>-<pid>-<random>`.
  2. Write all archive files into the staging directory, validating that each destination is
     inside it.
  3. Write a `.bifrost-skill.json` marker (schema v1, `source: "bifrost"`) containing
     `id`, `name`, optional `description`/`version`, `scope`, `directory`, `baseUrl`,
     `installedAt`, optional `updatedAt`, and `contentHash`.
  4. Rename the staging directory into the final location.
- Replacements (when allowed by `--force`/UI confirmation or an update) move the existing
  directory to a backup, swap the staging directory into place, then remove the backup
  best-effort.
- Refuse to overwrite an existing install without explicit force/confirmation.
- Treat directories that exist but lack a valid Bifrost marker as **foreign** and refuse
  installation without force.
- Compute a **SHA-256 content hash** over all files, sorted by relative path, as
  `name\0length\0bytes`, to drive update/unchanged decisions and auditing.
- Set file modes by content heuristic: files starting with a shebang (`#!`) are written
  `0755`; all other files are written `0644`.
- Persist an install record in plugin storage keyed by
  `installed:<scope>:<short dir hash>:<id>` as a secondary index; the on-disk marker remains
  the source of truth for recognition and safety.
- Trigger OpenCode's skill registry reload after successful installs, updates, or removals.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Crash-safe installs: failures leave the previous skill intact and clean up staging.
  - Clear provenance and safe detection of plugin-managed directories.
  - Accurate no-op detection during updates; local drift is visible via content hash.
- **Negative**
  - Whole-directory replacement semantics; local edits inside an installed skill are not
    merged and are lost on replace/update.
  - The storage index can drift (for example if the filesystem is manipulated) but is
    non-authoritative.
- **Risk**
  - Concurrent installs into the same target are not explicitly lock-coordinated; unique
    staging names avoid name collisions but do not serialize the operations.

# ADR-0008: Use conservative update and removal semantics

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Users need to refresh installed skills from the gateway without unexpected downgrades or
surprises. Installed skill directories may be edited locally; automatic merging is complex
and error-prone. Removal is destructive and must never delete arbitrary or foreign paths.

## Decision

- **Update:**
  - Target installed Bifrost records; default to `all` when no skill name is provided.
  - When both remote and installed versions are parseable as semantic versions, skip the
    update if the remote version is older.
  - Download the current archive and compare its **content hash** with the installed marker's
    hash; if identical, report the skill as `unchanged`.
  - Apply updates through the same atomic commit path used for installs (see ADR-0007).
  - Preserve the original `installedAt` and set `updatedAt` on replacement.
  - No merging of local edits: an update/replace overwrites the entire skill directory.
- **Remove:**
  - Only delete directories that satisfy all of the following:
    - They are direct children of a known skills root.
    - Their basename matches the resolved skill id/name.
    - They contain a valid Bifrost marker whose `id` matches the target.
  - Require `--global` or `--project` when the same skill exists in both scopes.
  - Remove the corresponding plugin storage entry and reload the registry.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Predictable, auditable behavior; prevents silent downgrades and accidental deletion of
    unmanaged files.
  - Content-hash comparison ensures updates are meaningful rather than merely re-applying the
    same files.
- **Negative**
  - Local customizations inside installed skills are lost on update or replacement; this must
    be documented and accepted by users.
- **Tradeoff**
  - Version comparison is best-effort (non-semver strings are treated as incomparable), so
    the content hash is the decisive signal for "no change".

# ADR-0009: Resolve configuration with precedence, normalization, and secret handling

- **Status:** Superseded by ADR-0012
- **Amended:** 2026-11-16
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Gateways differ per environment. Users need sensible defaults, per-install settings,
environment-based configuration for CI/development, and one-off command overrides.

Base URLs may be pasted in varying forms.

## Decision

- **Precedence (highest → lowest):**
  1. Command/call overrides (passed by the TUI/RPC for a single invocation).
  2. Plugin storage (written by `/bifrost-config`).
  3. Plugin options (from the OpenCode `plugins` config).
  4. Environment variables (`BIFROST_URL`, `BIFROST_TIMEOUT_MS`).
  5. Defaults (`http://localhost:8080`, `20000` ms).
- **Persistence:**
  - Store mutable settings in plugin storage under a `settings` key:
    - `baseUrl` (string)
    - `timeoutMs` (number)
  - Support `--reset` to clear stored settings.
- **URL normalization:**
  - Trim input; infer `http://` when a scheme is missing.
  - Accept only `http:` and `https:`.
  - Reject URLs containing embedded credentials (use `baseUrl` instead).
  - Remove trailing slashes and strip a trailing `/api` segment so a pasted
    `https://host/api` does not produce `https://host/api/api`.
- **Reporting:**
  - `/bifrost-config` and the TUI display the effective settings with source attribution
    (`command`, `storage`, `options`, `environment`, `default`) and the global skills
    directory path.
  - `timeoutMs` must be greater than zero; invalid values are rejected.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Flexible, transparent configuration with safe defaults.
  - No secret exposure in output and config files.
  - Tolerant of how users paste base URLs.
- **Negative**
  - Legacy management keys stored in plugin storage are automatically scrubbed on first read.

# ADR-0010: Provide forgiving slash commands with non-model transcript reporting

- **Status:** Superseded by ADR-0012 and ADR-0013
- **Amended:** 2026-11-16
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

Commands are used interactively in chat. Users expect flexible flag and option spellings,
clear immediate feedback, and deterministic tool-like behavior that does not wake the model.

OpenCode provides a mechanism for plugins to register commands and append synthetic messages
to a session transcript.

## Decision

- Register non-interactive slash commands in the server part:
  - `/bifrost-install <skill> [--project] [--force]`
  - `/bifrost-list`
  - `/bifrost-update [<skill>|all] [--global|--project]`
  - `/bifrost-remove <skill> [--global|--project]`
  - `/bifrost-config [options] [--reset]`
  - ~~`/bifrost-install-all [--project] [--force]`~~ — merged into
    `/bifrost-install [<skill>|all]` by ADR-0013.
- The interactive catalog browser lives in the TUI as `/bifrost-skills`.
- Parse arguments with a tolerant tokenizer/parser (`src/args.ts`):
  - Accept `--kebab-case`, `camelCase`, and bare `key=value` forms.
  - Provide aliases (`baseUrl`/`--base-url`/`--url`,
    `timeoutMs`/`--timeout-ms`, etc.).
  - Respect quoted values and a `--` terminator.
  - Treat known options as boolean flags and support `readScope`, `readBoolean`,
    `readString`, `readTimeout` helpers.
- Default behaviors:
  - Install commands default to `global`.
  - `/bifrost-update` defaults to `all`.
  - Commands report results via `format.ts` helpers producing Markdown.
- Report outcomes:
  - Emit a `notice` event to the TUI (toast).
  - Append a **synthetic session message** (resume disabled) with the formatted result so it
    appears in chat history without triggering model inference.
- **Tombstone:** If the user provides `apiKey`, `--api-key`, `--token`, `clearApiKey` or
  `clear-api-key`, the `/bifrost-config` command fails with a clear message: “API keys are no
  longer supported: Bifrost skill routes are public. Remove `apiKey` from your plugin options
  and unset `BIFROST_API_KEY`.”

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Low-friction, composable UX for scriptable or manual use.
  - Consistent output formatting across commands.
  - Results are visible in history without adding model turns.
  - No API keys or credentials required for any operation.
- **Negative**
  - Flexible parsing can accept ambiguous inputs; canonicalization rules must be maintained and
    tested.
  - Old command inputs with `apiKey` now fail; users must remove them.
- **Tradeoff**
  - Rich interactivity is concentrated in `/bifrost-skills` (TUI), while other commands remain
    non-interactive and easy to reason about.

# ADR-0011: Use minimal runtime dependencies and Bun-native tooling

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-16
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

The plugin performs ZIP extraction, YAML frontmatter parsing, and integration with OpenCode
APIs. It must keep its bundle and runtime simple, minimize supply-chain surface, and provide
fast, deterministic tests for filesystem/network/ZIP edge cases.

OpenCode runs on Bun, so aligning the development and test tooling with the runtime avoids
extra transpilation steps and behavior differences.

## Decision

- **Runtime dependencies (minimal):**
  - `@opencode/plugin` (host integration and typed RPC).
  - `fflate` (ZIP decode/inflate).
  - `yaml` (frontmatter parsing).
  - Use platform `fetch`, `node:fs`, `node:crypto`, and `node:path` rather than heavier HTTP
    or filesystem libraries.
- **Development dependencies:**
  - `@biomejs/biome` for linting/formatting.
  - `typescript` for type checking (`noEmit`).
  - `@types/bun` and `@types/node` for typing.
- **Testing/tooling:**
  - Use Bun's built-in test runner (`bun test`).
  - Prefer in-memory storage and mocked gateway implementations for most tests, with
    targeted real-local cases where necessary.
  - Cover arguments parsing, Bifrost client fallbacks and error handling, ZIP safety, settings
    precedence, operations (install/list/update/remove), and server plugin behavior.
- **Quality gates:**
  - `npm run check` runs Biome, TypeScript, and the test suite.
  - CI badge/workflow should run the same checks on push/PRs.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Small dependency footprint and clear control over security-sensitive logic (downloads,
    ZIP handling, install paths).
  - Fast feedback loop aligned with Bun's runtime behavior.
- **Negative**
  - More bespoke implementation (HTTP error handling, streaming caps, path normalization,
    install atomicity) to own and maintain compared to higher-level libraries.
- **Risk**
  - Correctness of edge-case handling depends on dedicated tests; regressions in timeouts,
    streaming caps, or path validation must be caught by the suite.

# ADR-0013: Unified install slash command

- **Status:** Proposed (implemented)
- **Date:** 2026-11-17
- **Deciders:** Maintainers of `@bitexpert/opencode-bifrost-skills`

## Context

The plugin previously exposed two separate slash commands for installing skills:

- `/bifrost-install <skill>` — installs a single skill by name
- `/bifrost-install-all` — installs every skill served by the gateway

Users had to remember which command to use depending on their goal, and the
duplicated behavior made the command surface area larger than necessary.

The update command already follows a selector pattern:

- `/bifrost-update [<skill>|all]` — defaults to `all` when no selector is given

We wanted to adopt the same convention for install to keep the UX consistent.

## Decision

- **Unify** `/bifrost-install` and `/bifrost-install-all` into a single command.
- **Selector semantics:**
  - No argument, `all`, or `*` → batch install (all skills)
  - Any other name → single install by that name
- **Flags stay the same:** `--global` / `--project`, `--force`
- **RPC and internal operations remain unchanged:** `install` and `installAll` are
  still separate methods; only the slash-command executor dispatches based on the
  selector.
- **The old `/bifrost-install-all` command is removed** from slash registration.

## Consequences

- **Positive**
  - Single command to remember: `/bifrost-install` covers both use cases.
  - Consistent with `/bifrost-update`'s selector convention.
  - Simplified command registration and maintenance.
  - No breaking changes for RPC consumers or internal operations.
- **Negative**
  - A skill literally named `all` or `*` can no longer be installed by name
    (only via batch).
  - Users relying on `/bifrost-install-all` must switch to `/bifrost-install`
    with the appropriate selector (which is a one-character change for most
    workflows).
- **Tradeoff**
  - The risk of "name collision" with `all` or `*` is minimal because Bifrost
    skills use kebab-case names, but the documentation must clarify the
    sentinel values.

## Migration guide

| Old command                      | New equivalent               |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `/bifrost-install-all`           | `/bifrost-install`           |
| `/bifrost-install-all --project` | `/bifrost-install --project` |
| `/bifrost-install-all --force`   | `/bifrost-install --force`   |

## Notes

- The RPC contract (`install`, `installAll` methods) and `Operations.install`,
  `Operations.installAll` are intentionally unchanged to avoid touching the TUI
  or other consumers.
- The sentinel `*` is supported via the existing tokenizer which treats it as a
  regular positional token.
- This change was made while the plugin is pre-1.0 (`0.1.0`) to keep semver
  breaking-change expectations clear.
